title: PSV-14 Effect of sericea lespedeza (lespedeza cuneata) on gastrointestinal nematode parasite egg count, body weight and scrotal circumference in weaned beef calves
content:
Abstract
Sericea lespedeza (SL) has been shown to reduce gastrointestinal nematode (GIN) parasite fecal egg counts (FEC) in small ruminants, and, in preliminary studies, SL had positive impacts on reproductive measures in intact male goats. However, little is known about the effect of SL on gastrointestinal and reproductive measures in cattle. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine possible effects of sericea lespedeza on gastrointestinal nematode (GIN) parasite fecal egg counts, body weight, and scrotal circumference in beef cattle. Sixteen mixed-sex (8 intact males, 8 females) Black Angus weaned calves at 9.0 ± 0.17 months of age and 305 ± 7 kg body weight (BW) were used. Calves were housed separately by sex in individual paddocks approximately 0.4 hectares in size consisting of dormant forages with two calves/paddock (n=4 paddocks/treatment). Animals were randomly allocated to treatment (n=4 of each sex/treatment) for similar preliminary body weights and GIN fecal egg counts (FEC). Animals were provided with a diet consisting of 50:50 bermudagrass hay and supplemental ration (both pre-weighed and fed daily) at up to 2.5% BW on a dry matter basis, adjusted weekly, for six weeks. The supplemental rations consisted of sericea lespedeza (SL), or commercial alfalfa pellets (CON) mixed with a commercial beef ration to meet (average 60% TDN/energy) or exceed (12% crude protein) nutritional requirements for moderate growth when combined with the hay. Animal BW was measured weekly. In addition, fecal samples were collected weekly by rectal grab from individual animals for analysis of GIN eggs per gram (epg) of feces using a modified McMaster’s technique with a sensitivity of 8 epg. Scrotal circumference was measured at the start (Week 0) and end of the study (Week 6). Data were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated data. There was no effect of treatment or time (week) on fecal egg counts or scrotal circumference. For the six weeks of the study, fecal egg counts averaged 539 ± 54 epg and 355 ± 32 epg, and scrotal circumference averaged 28.2 ± 0.5 cm and 28.4 ± 0.8 cm for CON and SL treated animals, respectively. Body weight was not influenced by treatment but tended to increase (P=0.0534) over time from 306 ± 7.4 kg to 328 ± 7.4 kg from Week 0 to Week 6 (average for all animals). Under the conditions of this study, there was no impact of sericea lespedeza on fecal egg counts, animal body weight or scrotal circumference
